This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:
 ORDER Case diary is available.

This is first application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C for grant of bail to the applicant as he has been arrested on 29.05.2023 in connection with Crime No.96/2023 registered at Police Station Vijaypur, District Guna for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 458, 506 of IPC.
Prosecution story, in brief, is that, in the intervening night of 25.05.2023 and 26.05.2023, applicant entered into the house of prosecutrix and threatened her and committed rape on her.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that prosecutrix is a major lady aged about 26 years.
She in her statements recorded during investigation under Section 164 of Cr.P.C has no where stated that applicant committed sexual intercourse with her.

The offence punishable under Section 376 of Mushtak Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194394182/
1 IPC is not made out against him.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He is in custody since 29.05.2023 and the trial will take time to conclude, therefore, in the aforesaid circumstances, applicant is entitled for grant of bail.

Learned counsel for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the prayer and submits that prosecutrix in the FIR and her statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C has specifically made allegations against the applicant that he forcefully committed rape with her.
The offence alleged against applicant is serious in nature, therefore, he is not entitled for bail.
Heard the learned counsel for both the parties.

Having considered rival submissions, age of prosecutrix, her statement recorded during investigation under Section 164 of Cr.P.C and other facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail, hence the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during the pendency of trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr.P.C.
M.Cr.C. stands disposed of, accordingly.

(SATYENDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE Aman Mushtak Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194394182/
